name: Pyrogranite tile
summary: A hard, frost-proof ceramic that the Zsolnay factory made from 1886. It is fired at a very high heat and carries a strong glaze, so that it can face roofs and walls.
how: Mix a stoneware clay with grog and press it into a mould.
Fire the body at 1200 to 1300 °C until it is dense.
Apply a coloured glaze and fire it again.
Hang the tile on battens or set it in mortar on the wall.

origin.note: The Zsolnay factory develops pyrogranite, a frost-proof body for architectural ceramics.

adoptions.via: Ödön Lechner and the Zsolnay factory use pyrogranite tile and relief for the roofs and facades of Budapest.
